meaning: to argue a position you may not really hold, in order to test the strength of an idea
literal_translation: pełnić rolę adwokata diabła (przedstawiać przeciwny punkt widzenia, by sprawdzić argumenty)
example: In our seminar, Mark played devil's advocate to test the strength of our arguments.
origin: From the Catholic Church, where an official argued against a candidate for sainthood to examine the case carefully

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to believe in any religion
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with religious belief itself; the word 'devil' is only part of its historical origin.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to make a very risky bet
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes arguing a point in discussion, not taking financial or personal risks.
The idiom means taking part in a discussion by arguing the opposite side, so it is the opposite of avoiding debate.

explanation: 'Play devil's advocate' means to present the opposite view on purpose, so that an idea can be tested and strengthened. It is useful in argumentative essays when you want to address counter-arguments.
